title: Hall Taco Bar Night
seoTitle: Hall Taco Bar Night | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Build-your-own tacos at the table
description: Build-your-own tacos at the table. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Prep toppings
steps.instruction: Dice onion, pick cilantro leaves, cut limes into wedges. Warm a sheet tray for holding cooked protein — tacos move fast once meat hits the board.

steps.title: Cook the filling
steps.instruction: Season protein with salt and cumin. Sear over medium-high until cooked through (chicken 165°F, steak 130°F then rest). Rest steak 8 minutes; slice thin against the grain.

steps.title: Warm tortillas
steps.instruction: Char tortillas on a dry griddle 20 seconds per side or wrap in foil at 300°F 10 minutes. Stack in a towel so they stay pliable.

steps.title: Run the taco line
steps.instruction: Hall Taco Bar Night: protein, onion, cilantro, lime. Crew builds their own — fastest way to feed eight without cold plates.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Warm tortillas in a dry skillet stack — wrap in foil so the line stays soft.
Set proteins, salsa, and toppings in separate bowls for build-your-own station flow.
Line up Hall Taco Bar Night on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Build-your-own tacos at the table. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
